title: Assignment 1: Build a training-score report
instructions: Modules 1–3: Python basics, installation, loops and sequences. Review a small training-score script, choose valid terminal commands, and complete its calculations and iteration logic. Answer all eight questions in this page; running an external editor is not required during the timed assignment.

questions.prompt: The report stores a score as score = 80. Which expression produces a number equal to 90?
What does this discount helper return?
You saved report.py on Windows. Which command runs it from the terminal?
Why create a virtual environment for this reporting project?
options: To automatically fix all syntax errors

questions.prompt: Which slice selects only 72 and 90?
What list is produced by the report filter?
questions.code:
scores = [60, 72, 90, 95]
passed = [s for s in scores if s >= 75]

questions.prompt: Choose the output for this numbered report.
questions.code:
for number, score in enumerate([72, 90], start=1):
    print(number, score)

questions.prompt: An employee has no scores yet. Which change prevents division by zero?
options: Check that scores is nonempty before dividing
Replace / with // and keep an empty list

title: Assignment 2: Validate an employee settings record
instructions: Modules 4–6: dictionaries, sets and modules; configuration manager; error handling. Complete and debug a settings validator. Focus on duplicate keys, data validation, safe updates and narrow exception handling.

questions.prompt: Which result removes duplicate skills while preserving all distinct skill values?
Which lookup returns 'light' when the theme key is absent without adding the key?
What does the second call return when add_setting normalizes keys and refuses duplicates?
Which update correctly leaves a missing key unchanged?
options: Check key in settings, then assign only if present
Assign settings[key] without a membership check
Clear the dictionary before every update
Always insert the missing key twice

questions.prompt: Which exception should this conversion handler catch for text equal to 'many'?
The conversion int('0') succeeds. What additional check is needed for a positive count?
options: Check that text is a dictionary

questions.prompt: Which validation rejects both a missing name and a non-string name?
A helper lives in checks.py as valid_record. Which statement imports that function?

title: Assignment 3: Review a budget and media model
instructions: Modules 7–9: classes and objects; budget ledger; object-oriented programming. Review per-instance state, transaction accounting, transfer behavior and shared interfaces. Select the implementation decisions that preserve each model's invariants.

questions.prompt: Where should a Budget create its mutable entries list so different accounts are independent?
options: entries = [] once in the class body
In a shared global list for all budgets

questions.prompt: What quantity is printed?
A ledger stores integer cents. What is the balance in cents?
questions.code:
entries = [(2500, 'deposit'), (-650, 'lunch')]
balance = sum(c for c, note in entries)

questions.prompt: A transfer lacks enough funds. What should happen?
options: Return failure and leave both ledgers unchanged
Credit the recipient before checking funds

questions.prompt: Which design supports encapsulation of salary changes?
options: A property setter that rejects negative pay
Let every caller bypass all validation
Store all salaries in one unrelated global variable

questions.prompt: Audio and Video both implement duration(). Calling duration on either through the same interface demonstrates what?
What happens when a subclass does not implement a required abstract method?
options: Instantiating that incomplete subclass raises TypeError
Python silently supplies the correct method
The method becomes a dictionary key

questions.prompt: Why use integer cents for the practice budget?
options: To avoid binary floating-point rounding surprises in money calculations
To prevent all possible input errors without validation

title: Assignment 4: Design a shape inventory and lookup table
instructions: Modules 10–12: polygon calculator; linear data structures; hash table. Check shape invariants and fitting calculations, choose stack or queue behavior, and handle hash collisions without losing records.

questions.prompt: How many 2 by 2 rectangles fit into an 8 by 3 rectangle without rotation?
A Square exposes a side setter. What invariant must it preserve?
options: Width and height remain equal and positive
Every square must have the same area

questions.prompt: Which value is removed from this stack?
Enrollment requests must be processed in arrival order. Which structure and operation are appropriate?
options: list with pop() at the end

questions.prompt: What special case must a singly linked list handle when deleting its first node?
options: Update the head reference to the next node
Require a predecessor that does not exist

questions.prompt: Two distinct keys map to the same hash-table bucket. What should separate chaining do?
options: Keep both entries and compare original keys during lookup
Treat equal bucket indexes as equal keys
Reject every second entry in the table

questions.prompt: Putting an existing key with a new value should do what?
options: Update that key's entry without creating a duplicate
Change every key in the table

questions.prompt: Why create buckets with a comprehension rather than [[]] * size?
options: Each bucket must own a separate mutable list
All buckets must share exactly one list

title: Assignment 5: Trace a search and recursive move planner
instructions: Modules 13–15: recursion; searching and sorting; Tower of Hanoi. Trace call results, choose stopping conditions, verify a binary search interval and check the move count and legal-move constraints of a recursive puzzle solver.

questions.prompt: What is the result of total_to(3)?
Which two properties make this recursion terminate for nonnegative integers?
options: A base case at zero and decreasing n on each call
Adding one to n on each call without a stop

questions.prompt: What input requirement does binary search depend on?
options: The values are sorted in the ordering used for comparisons
The list length is a power of two

questions.prompt: When values[mid] is less than the target in ascending binary search, which update is correct?
Which description matches merge sort?
options: Divide the input and merge sorted halves
Always select a random unsorted answer
Use a queue without comparing values

questions.prompt: What is the minimum number of moves to solve Tower of Hanoi with three disks?
Which move violates Tower of Hanoi rules?
options: Put a larger disk on a smaller disk
Move one disk to an empty peg
Put a smaller disk on a larger disk
Move one top disk at a time

questions.prompt: Before moving the largest disk from source to target, where must the smaller n-1 disks go?
options: Under the largest disk on the source
Onto the target and remain there
They must be removed from the puzzle

title: Assignment 6: Plan routes and verify a learning catalogue
instructions: Modules 16–18: graphs and trees; dynamic programming; review and capstone. Choose graph traversal behavior, reuse overlapping results and review catalogue validation and skill-counting tests. Passing this final assignment is required for course completion.

questions.prompt: Which traversal finds a shortest path measured in number of edges in an unweighted graph?
options: Any depth-first path is always shortest

questions.prompt: Why mark a vertex visited when it is enqueued during breadth-first search?
options: To prevent duplicate queue entries and repeated visits through cycles
To ensure the graph has no edges
To make every graph into a tree

questions.prompt: What does memoization add to a recursive solution?
options: A cache of previously computed subproblem results
A requirement to use global mutable lists

questions.prompt: What does fibonacci(6) return?

options: Each next value depends only on its two predecessors
Python stores an invisible full table automatically

options: To count a repeated skill only once for that employee
To convert skill names to numbers

questions.prompt: Which test set best covers a skill-counting helper?
options: Normal records, empty records, duplicate skills and invalid records
Only printed output with no expected value
No checks because dictionaries cannot contain mistakes

questions.prompt: Which architecture keeps the capstone easier to test?
options: Separate input validation, core logic and presentation
Mix every input prompt into each calculation
